cases.purpose: Primary provenance remains independent from named dependencies, support status, and execution coverage.
Naming a dependency does not promote an Engine-attested fact to profile-verified provenance.
Support status does not promote an offchain-derived fact to Core-verified provenance.
Core-verified provenance requires the exact Core identity, authenticated invocation context, and authenticated event schema.
A valid Core-shaped record from another deployment is not evidence from the expected Core.
A matching Core identity without an authenticated invocation context is insufficient.
An unauthenticated event schema cannot carry Core-verified provenance.
An Engine cannot create a Core Receipt by copying its discriminator or event shape.
A post-callback checkpoint may establish final Engine-state evidence.
A binding proof that no later call can reach the state may establish finality without another checkpoint.
A pre-settlement state is not final while a later untrusted callback can mutate it.
An atomic normalized Receipt carries its identity inputs, exact committed relationships, evidence axes, assessment state, opaque Engine output, and plan commitment.
A Receipt cannot change the committed protected Effect type while retaining the same occurrence identity and valid references.
A Receipt cannot re-associate a protected Effect with other valid Targets, Scopes, positions, dependencies, or evidence references.
A bounded-session normalized Receipt carries every ordered segment commitment and the final zero-obligation checkpoint in addition to the common portable fields.
A schema-complete Receipt is incomplete when it omits one committed Execution Target from the ordered target tuple.
A Receipt cannot associate a committed Execution Target with a different Market.
A Receipt cannot substitute a Principal Scope or report a different committed fill sequence.
A schema-complete Receipt must contain the full record for every applicable Protocol Assessment group, including a zero-valued group.
A bounded-session Receipt cannot substitute a different final zero-obligation checkpoint while retaining the committed transcript identity.
An applicable debit that floors to zero still produces a keyed zero-valued assessment record.
When no applicable debit exists, the assessment group and its record are absent.
Omitting the record for an applicable zero-valued assessment loses the distinction from an absent group.
A Receipt cannot emit an assessment group when no applicable debit exists.
A bounded-session Receipt preserves exact segment order, the final transcript digest, and zero remaining obligations.
Reordering otherwise identical segments invalidates bounded-session receipt reconstruction.
The Receipt final transcript digest must match the digest computed from the ordered transcript.
A bounded session cannot commit while any temporary obligation remains nonzero.
A bounded-session Receipt must contain its final zero-obligation checkpoint.
